Article 7

(1) The basic policy as referred to in Article 6 is elaborated in the Regional Action Plan.

(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is integrated with the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, Regional Medium-Term Development Plan and Regional Government Work Plan documents.

(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) at a minimum contains:

a. action programs and activities for the protection of women and children, including women and children victims of violence;
b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. action programs and activities for the improvement and enhancement of protection services for women and children victims of violence; and
d. action programs and activities for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 29

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors.

(2) Social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide services to women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 28

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services from Health Facilities in accordance with their professional standards.

(2) In the event that women and children victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obligated to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.

(3) The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 18

(1) In the event that women and children victims of violence require continuous treatment, women and children victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 26

(1) Assistance shall be provided by individuals or institutions having the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.

(2) Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

For the purposes of recovery, women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence may obtain services from:

a. Social institutions (groups or institutions having scope in women and children) and or;
b. Social workers (Individuals having competence to conduct recovery or rehabilitation) namely:
1. Nurses
2. Health workers

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

That protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, so that regulation is needed as a basis for the provision of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

Article 29

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors.

(2) Social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide services to women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 35

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children, both conducted by PPT and non-governmental organizations.

(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in the framework of realizing the objectives of implementing protection of women and children in accordance with the mechanisms and service procedures established in laws and regulations.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Agency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 28

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services from Health Facilities in accordance with their professional standards.

(2) In the event that women and children victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obligated to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.

(3) The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Paragraph 4

Scope

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 18

(1) In the event that women and children victims of violence require continuous treatment, women and children victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 9

(1) The Regent is obligated to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.

(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

CONCERNING

THE PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

That protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, so that regulation is needed as a basis for the provision of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

General

Article 18

(1) In the event that women and children victims of violence require continuous treatment, women and children victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 45

(1) Every person who violates the prohibitions as referred to in Article 41 and Article 42 shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) The criminal acts as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are violations.

Article 6

The Regent establishes basic policies for the implementation of protection of women and children in the Region.

Article 35

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children, both conducted by PPT and non-governmental organizations.

(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in the framework of realizing the objectives of implementing protection of women and children in accordance with the mechanisms and service procedures established in laws and regulations.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Agency.

Paragraph 3

Rights of Witnesses and Perpetrators

Part Three

Special Protection of Children

Article 14

Neglect as referred to in Article 10 letter d is caused by: a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of the child, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after the child properly committed by parents, guardians or any other party responsible for their care; c. acts of neglecting persons within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such persons; and/or

d. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 9

(1) The Regent is obligated to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.

(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

1.9.text:
Article 15

Exploitation as referred to in Article 10 letter e is caused by: a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of the physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to gain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to gain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 7

(1) The basic policy as referred to in Article 6 is elaborated in the Regional Action Plan.

(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is integrated with the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, Regional Medium-Term Development Plan and Regional Government Work Plan documents.

(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) at a minimum contains:

a. action programs and activities for the protection of women and children, including women and children victims of violence;
b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. action programs and activities for the improvement and enhancement of protection services for women and children victims of violence; and
d. action programs and activities for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 6

The Regent establishes basic policies for the implementation of protection of women and children in the Region.

Article 35

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children, both conducted by PPT and non-governmental organizations.

(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in the framework of realizing the objectives of implementing protection of women and children in accordance with the mechanisms and service procedures established in laws and regulations.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Agency.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 32

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this regional regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Probolinggo Regency.

Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 27

For the purposes of recovery, women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence may obtain services from:

a. Social institutions (groups or institutions having scope in women and children) and or;
b. Social workers (Individuals having competence to conduct recovery or rehabilitation) namely:
1. Nurses
2. Health workers

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 37

Provisions regarding guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4

The Regional Government is obligated to implement the protection of women and children.

Article 32

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this regional regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Probolinggo Regency.

CONCERNING

THE PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

That protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, so that regulation is needed as a basis for the provision of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

Article 43

(1) Health Workers who refuse or are unwilling to provide health examination services as referred to in Article 28 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:

a. written warning;
b. suspension of practice license/work permit;
c. restriction of practice for Health Workers in independent practice; (2) Social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors who refuse or are unwilling to provide counseling services as referred to in Article 29 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of: a. reprimand; or
b. written warning.
(3) Provisions regarding the mechanism for imposing sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

3.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Part Two

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence

Article 29

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors.

(2) Social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide services to women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 28

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services from Health Facilities in accordance with their professional standards.

(2) In the event that women and children victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obligated to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.

(3) The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7

(1) The basic policy as referred to in Article 6 is elaborated in the Regional Action Plan.

(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is integrated with the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, Regional Medium-Term Development Plan and Regional Government Work Plan documents.

(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) at a minimum contains:

a. action programs and activities for the protection of women and children, including women and children victims of violence;
b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. action programs and activities for the improvement and enhancement of protection services for women and children victims of violence; and
d. action programs and activities for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 18

(1) In the event that women and children victims of violence require continuous treatment, women and children victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 42

PPT operators or safe houses are prohibited from charging fees in providing services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence.

Article 9

(1) The Regent is obligated to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.

(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

Article 32

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this regional regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Probolinggo Regency.

Article 21

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 26

(1) Assistance shall be provided by individuals or institutions having the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 28

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services from Health Facilities in accordance with their professional standards.

(2) In the event that women and children victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obligated to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.

(3) The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 29

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors.

(2) Social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide services to women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 26

(1) Assistance shall be provided by individuals or institutions having the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.

(2) Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 18

(1) In the event that women and children victims of violence require continuous treatment, women and children victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

That protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, so that regulation is needed as a basis for the provision of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children in a Regional Regulation.

(1) The Regional Government may provide funding assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement protection of women and children.

b. services; and

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 6

The Regent establishes basic policies for the implementation of protection of women and children in the Region.

Article 29

(1) Women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors.

(2) Social workers, companion volunteers, and/or spiritual advisors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide services to women and children victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 8

The Regional Action Plan must be used as a guideline for the Regional Government in formulating policies related to the implementation of protection of women and children.

Article 33

In implementing protection of women and children, individuals, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and business entities shall coordinate with PPT.

Article 20

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential treatment, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

(2) Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Special Protection of Children

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 35

(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in the framework of realizing the objectives of implementing protection of women and children in accordance with the mechanisms and service procedures established in laws and regulations.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Agency.

Article 37

Provisions regarding guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 6

The Regent establishes basic policies for the implementation of protection of women and children in the Region.

Article 14

Neglect as referred to in Article 10 letter d is caused by: a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of the child, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after the child properly committed by parents, guardians or any other party responsible for their care; c. acts of neglecting persons within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such persons; and/or

d. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

Article 21

Protection of women and children victims of violence includes:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 38

(1) PPT is obligated to report the implementation of protection of women and children to the Regent through the Agency.

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 24

(1) Empowerment as referred to in Article 21 letter c is organized through:

a. job training;
b. productive economic business and joint business groups; and c. capital assistance.
(2) Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a includes: a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.
(3) Productive economic business and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include:
a. entrepreneurial skills training; and
b. business actor assistance.
(4) Capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c includes: a. assistance for facilities and infrastructure; and
b. working/business capital assistance facilities.
(5) Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PPT.

CONCERNING

THE PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

That protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, so that regulation is needed as a basis for the provision of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

Article 24

(1) Empowerment as referred to in Article 21 letter c is organized through:

a. job training;
b. productive economic business and joint business groups; and c. capital assistance.
(2) Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a includes: a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.
(3) Productive economic business and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include:
a. entrepreneurial skills training; and
b. business actor assistance.
(4) Capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c includes: a. assistance for facilities and infrastructure; and
b. working/business capital assistance facilities.
(5) Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PPT.

Article 26

(1) Assistance shall be provided by individuals or institutions having the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.

(2) Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 36

(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on: a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for protection of women and children; and

b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 9

(1) The Regent is obligated to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.

(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

Part Four

Assistance

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protection of women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in the effort to empower women in various fields of development as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age or a child who is suspected, accused, convicted, and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
